Row 1: Held the field.Event: **The Department of Improvement** names the battle an improvement, in writing, with a stamp
Row 1: Held the field.Accept: It goes in the annual report, in a font nobody chose, and the Department sends a commemorative copy item worth up to 3 parts: gain it
Row 1: Held the field.Pay: Pay **1 part** for the frame and the photographer: one fighter wears the badge into the next battle **Under warranty** (the badge is official), and the photographer talks: gain a **lead**
Row 1: Held the field.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): your speech from a crate keeps the printer to the end, and he becomes your contact **Fixer** and leaves a copy item worth up to 3 parts / you read the page on fire exits, and the Department takes back one copy item

Row 1: Held the field.Event: **Hollowood wants the rights.** A producer in a very clean coat has brought a contract, and a smile
Row 1: Held the field.Accept: They send a courtesy copy of the film, with a note thanking you for your cooperation: gain one copy item worth up to 3 parts
Row 1: Held the field.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for a lawyer who finds a hole in the contract, and a buyer for the props: gain a **lead**, and the contact **Fence** (the lawyer sells the props)
Row 1: Held the field.Twist: Shoot: they want your best shot again, for the camera, with the producer watching, and you hit it: roll on the **finds** table / you miss on camera, and the film makes you the villains: lose a **contact**, a prop-house friend who saw the cut

Row 1: Held the field.Event: **A crowd of bettors** owes the crew. They bet against you and lost, and are being very friendly about it
Row 1: Held the field.Accept: 4 parts, counted out slowly, in small coins
Row 1: Held the field.Twist: Fight: you collect in person, with one hand flat on the table: roll on the **finds** table / they had friends, and you swear you'll be back: you leave with nothing, and gain **Oathbreakers**

Row 1: Held the field.Event: **The loot is stamped.** An Inspectorate clerk has found a mark on it, and wants a fee
Row 1: Held the field.Accept: Pay 4 parts or lose one copy item, and the clerk writes you a receipt either way
Row 1: Held the field.Pay: Slide the clerk **1 part** under the form: the stamp is waved through, and you pay nothing else
Row 1: Held the field.Twist: Tech: you forge a stamp, a good one, and keep everything / the clerk knows his own stamp: pay 8

Row 1: Held the field.Event: **A drifter saw it all** from behind a wreck, and wants to join. They have brought their own kettle
Row 1: Held the field.Accept: One rookie may be hired for 5 parts less; the drifter has opinions about the pay
Row 1: Held the field.Twist: Grit: they keep up on the walk home, so they are the real thing: hire them for 10 parts less (free at most) / they were running from someone: write that someone as a **rival**, and the drifter steals one item and leaves

Row 1: Held the field.Event: **Victory feast.** Somebody found a pot, and somebody else found what to put in it
Row 1: Held the field.Accept: The newest fighter gets a second helping, and a story to go with it: they start the next battle **Hyped**
Row 1: Held the field.Pay: Pay **5 parts** for the good table: up to five fighters start the next battle **Hyped**
Row 1: Held the field.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): your toast lands, and a patron at the next fire hears it: gain the contact **Patron**, and a copy item worth up to 2 parts / a fight breaks out over the toast, and a patron walks out: lose a **contact**

Row 2: Did not hold the field.Event: **The debt collector calls** from the Collections Department. He calls everyone friend. If the crew has a rival gang, the gang sent them, mob-handed
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Accept: He takes one copy item as a down payment, and writes you a receipt
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Pay: Cross off a **lead**: it tells you where the collector sleeps, and he goes away owing you a favour: gain the contact **Fixer**
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Twist: Fight (-1 die if a rival gang sent them): they leave, you take a copy item worth up to 3 parts off the field, and a rival gang is crossed off / you promise to pay next week, and don't: gain **Oathbreakers**, and recharging costs double this break

Row 2: Did not hold the field.Event: **Sympathy from a patron.** They come to the camp with a basket, to say how sorry they are
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Accept: Take the pity: 1 part, and two fighters start the next battle **Shook**
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Pay: Refuse the money and pay **2 parts** for the drinks: the patron sends a cousin who needs work, and one rookie may be hired for 5 parts less
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): "we don't need it", you say, and mean it, and the patron's driver names a cheap armourer: the first purchase this break costs **5 less** / you say the crew won't fight again without better odds: lose the **lead**, and the first purchase this break costs 3 more

Row 2: Did not hold the field.Event: **Scavengers on the field** after you left. Someone saw the smoke and brought a cart
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Accept: You let them keep it, and their cart blocks the charging point: recharging costs double this break
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Pay: Pay **3 parts**: a local guide finds the scavengers' camp, and you get back one item lost this battle
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Twist: Grit: you walk in and take it back, free: get one item lost this battle back / the cart is gone with the salvage: you lose two copy items

Row 2: Did not hold the field.Event: **A rookie loses heart.** They sit at the edge of the camp, looking at their hands
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Accept: The newest fighter (lowest Experience) loses one copy item they carried, **for good**: it leaves the crew's roster at once (the player picks which; with none, nothing happens)
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Pay: Pay **1 part**: a pep talk with drinks, and nothing else happens
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Twist: Grit: they shrug it off and gain +1 XP / they leave the crew in the night (their gear stays)

Row 2: Did not hold the field.Event: **The voice reviews the battle.** It has notes, and it wants to read them all
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Accept: The voice files a cheerful report, and it is the report the next buyer reads: the first purchase this break costs 2 more
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for an appeal: a technician fixes the report, and tells you who read it: gain a **lead**
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Twist: Tech: it finds a real lesson, +1 XP to one fighter, and gain a **lead** / it insists you won and files it: the crew pays 5 parts in fines

Row 2: Did not hold the field.Event: **Named on the boards.** The winners' victory speech names your captain, and spells it right
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Accept: The captain is **Sore**: they went to the board to argue, and the board won
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for the board space: the captain writes the reply, and the crew gains **Showboats**
Row 2: Did not hold the field.Twist: Shoot, Hard (10): one fighter shoots the captain's name off the board, and the camp talks: gain a **lead** and 4 parts / they miss, and the board names that too: the captain is **Sore** again, and the board-keeper stops taking your calls: lose a **contact**

Row 3: Ran.Event: **Word gets round.** Gawk's rumour board has your name on it, in chalk
Row 3: Ran.Pay: Pay **2 parts**: a quiet word with the rumour board, and no tag
Row 3: Ran.Twist: Fight: you say it to their faces, at the board, and the board is wrong: the board-keeper becomes your contact **Informer** / gain **Ran**, and recharging costs double this break

Row 3: Ran.Event: **The patron withholds pay** and keeps the deposit, and sends a very polite note. If the crew has a rival patron, it is them
Row 3: Ran.Accept: The patron blacklists you: lose a **contact**
Row 3: Ran.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for a lawyer's letter: they settle, nobody is cut off, and they pay the deposit back in kind: a copy item worth up to 3 parts
Row 3: Ran.Twist: Fight: they pay up after all, 5 parts, and if the patron was a rival it is crossed off: paid, and done with them / lose 2 parts, and gain Ran

Row 3: Ran.Event: **Shame.** Nobody says anything, which is worse
Row 3: Ran.Accept: One fighter that was evacuated starts the next battle **Shook** (nobody asked them to come back)
Row 3: Ran.Pay: Pay **1 part** for drinks: nobody says a word, and that fighter starts the next battle **Hyped** instead
Row 3: Ran.Twist: Grit, Routine (6): they are fine, and say so, and they start the next battle **Hyped** and **Under warranty** / it shows: gain **Ran**

Row 3: Ran.Event: **Wise retreat.** A Control Group observer notes it, in a very small hand
Row 3: Ran.Accept: The observer notes your cells for the study, and keeps the notes: write the observer on the roster as a **rival**
Row 3: Ran.Pay: Pay the observer **1 part** for a footnote: the paper cites you as careful, and the observer leaves a sample kit: a copy item worth up to 3 parts
Row 3: Ran.Twist: Tech, Hard (10): the paper cites you as the one crew that does what it says, and the field team sends a bonus: gain **Oathkeepers** and 4 parts / it calls you a control sample, gain Ran

Row 3: Ran.Event: **The evac pilot bills you.** He itemises the sky
Row 3: Ran.Pay: Give the pilot one copy item (the crew chooses): he waives the bill, and he knows a buyer: the first sale this break is at full price
Row 3: Ran.Twist: Tech: the bill has an error in your favour, and he refunds 2 parts / pay 6, and the pilot tells the dock why you called: gain **Ran**

Row 3: Ran.Event: **Someone else's pod.** An arrival from a pod nobody claimed wanders into your camp, in their good clothes
Row 3: Ran.Accept: The arrival steals 2 parts as they wander through
Row 3: Ran.Pay: Pay **1 part** for food: one rookie (Past "Unwritten") may be hired for 5 parts less
Row 3: Ran.Twist: Nerve: you tell them who they were, and they believe it: they join for 10 parts less, and the player picks their rumour now / they don't believe you, wander off, and take one copy item

Row 4: Lost someone.Event: **A funeral of tape.** They are wrapped in it, the Bodger way, and everyone brings a roll
Row 4: Lost someone.Accept: The crew stays by the body all night, and nobody sleeps: one fighter is **Sore**
Row 4: Lost someone.Pay: Pay **2 parts**: a quick one, with a short speech, and the stalls open on time. A mourner tells you who is asking after the dead: gain a **lead**
Row 4: Lost someone.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): someone gives the eulogy and it carries across the whole camp: +1 XP to the speaker, and a mourner becomes your contact **Patron** / the tape runs out mid-eulogy, and so does the eulogy: lose a **contact**, and recharging costs double this break

Row 4: Lost someone.Event: **An oath at the grave.** Somebody has to say it out loud
Row 4: Lost someone.Accept: One fighter kneels and writes a Big Word on their card now, a vow for the next battle (section 13.5)
Row 4: Lost someone.Twist: Grit: the whole crew swears, one after another: the crew may swear one more Word next battle, and gains **Oathkeepers** / nobody can speak: the crew swears no Words next battle, and the promise to the dead goes unsaid: gain **Oathbreakers**

Row 4: Lost someone.Event: **The wake.** Somebody found the good bottle, the one they were saving
Row 4: Lost someone.Accept: The crew drinks to them, and the bottle was not cheap: one fighter is **Sore** (the morning)
Row 4: Lost someone.Twist: Grit: someone drinks the rest under the table and tells the story right, and the camp goes quiet: the crew gains **Showboats** / it turns into a fight: lose one copy item (broken over a head), and one fighter starts the next battle **Shook**

Row 4: Lost someone.Event: **Their gear is claimed** by a creditor, who has brought the receipts and a cart
Row 4: Lost someone.Accept: Lose one item the lost fighter carried
Row 4: Lost someone.Pay: Write the creditor as a **rival**: keep it
Row 4: Lost someone.Twist: Fight: you stand in the way of the cart: keep it, and the creditor owes you: gain a **lead** / lose two items

Row 4: Lost someone.Event: **A relative turns up** to fill the space, with the same nose and a different surname
Row 4: Lost someone.Accept: Hire one rookie for 2 parts less, same species as the lost fighter
Row 4: Lost someone.Pay: Give them one item the lost fighter carried (the crew chooses): hire them for **10 parts less**
Row 4: Lost someone.Twist: Grit: they take the lost fighter's title with a prefix, and wear it well: hire them for 5 parts less, and they gain **+1 XP** / they want the lost fighter's gear, and say so: give them one item

Row 4: Lost someone.Event: **Revenge.** The enemy fighter who put them down is written on the roster as a **rival**
Row 4: Lost someone.Accept: Their name goes up on the wall, and everyone learns to say it
Row 4: Lost someone.Twist: Shoot: one fighter shoots the rival's picture off the boards and swears it: cross the rival off, and they start the next battle **Hyped** and **Under warranty** / they miss, and everyone saw: they start the next battle **Shook**, and the lead goes cold: lose the **lead**

Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Event: **The captive talked.** Nobody asked. It started, and then could not stop
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Accept: It points out a stash: gain one copy item worth up to 4 parts
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Pay: Pay **1 part**: you turn the captive into your contact **Informer**, and it points out a second stash: a copy item worth up to 5 parts
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Twist: Fight: you lean on it, gently at first: roll on the **finds** table / it lied, and you let it go anyway: lose the **lead** (it sold your route)

Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Event: **A threat from the captive's crew.** A note, in good handwriting, left on a post
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Accept: The crew sleeps behind the gate, and a night watchman talks: gain the contact **Informer**
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Pay: Pay **2 parts**: the threat is withdrawn, one rival is crossed off, the crew gains the contact **Fixer** (they mediate), and up to two fighters start the next battle **Hyped**
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Twist: Shoot, Hard (10): you send one back through their window, with a note of your own: gain a **lead** and 8 parts / you miss: lose 2 parts

Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Event: **The ransom was counterfeit** (if you received one). The ink is the wrong shade of green
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Accept: The ransom was worth nothing: write the forger on the roster as a **rival**
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Pay: Pay a notary **1 part** to check the stamps: he finds the forger, and the forger's lawyer pays the damages in kind: a copy item worth up to 3 parts
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Twist: Tech, Routine (6): the stamps are real, and the sender apologises at length: 4 parts / lose 6 parts

Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Event: **The paid-for fighter is grateful** (if you paid one). They keep trying to carry things
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Accept: The family of the paid-for fighter sends thanks, and a name: gain the contact **Fixer**
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): they swear to repay it, and mean it. They start **Hyped** and **Under warranty**, and gain +1 XP / they resent being bought: they start the next battle **Shook**

Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Event: **A reputation for business.** Word gets round that you ask a fair price and hand back what you sell
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Accept: The board reads well: the first purchase this break costs 3 less
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Pay: Pay **1 part** for a price list: merchants read it, and the crew gains the contact **Fence**, and a merchant sends a copy item worth up to 5 parts
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Twist: Tech: the price list works: the first purchase this break costs **5 less**, and a merchant sends a copy item worth up to 4 parts / a typo makes "ransoms" read "bodies", and a challenger comes looking: write them as a **rival**, and lose 3 parts

Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Event: **The Inspectorate wants paperwork.** A clerk with a clipboard and no sense of time
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Accept: The clerk takes the captive's papers and keeps a copy: write the clerk on the roster as a **rival**
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Pay: A bribe of **3 parts**: the clerk files the captive as "returned unharmed", nobody is written down, and he tells you what the next inspection will ask: gain a **lead**
Row 5: Took a captive or paid a ransom.Twist: Tech, Routine (6): the forms are in order, and the clerk likes you: gain a **lead** / pay 5 parts

Row 6: Made a legend.Event: **The song is wrong.** It is about someone else, and everybody sings it anyway
Row 6: Made a legend.Accept: The bard sells you the tune, and plays it at the charging point: recharge one fighter's battery by 3, free
Row 6: Made a legend.Pay: Pay **1 part**: the song is about the right fighter, the crew gains **Showboats**, and the bard becomes your contact **Informer**
Row 6: Made a legend.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): it is about you: the crew gains **Showboats**, and the legend gains +1 XP / it is about the enemy, and their crew gets famous: write them as a **rival**

Row 6: Made a legend.Event: **Fans.** A few of them, with pens
Row 6: Made a legend.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for printed pictures: the legend's picture is sold at the next camp, the crew gains **Showboats**, and the fans pass the hat: a copy item worth up to 5 parts
Row 6: Made a legend.Twist: Grit: the legend signs everything, all night, and the pens run dry: roll on the **finds** table / a fan walks off with a keepsake: the legend loses one item they carried, **for good** (the player chooses)

Row 6: Made a legend.Event: **A patron wants the legend** for a job, by name. If the crew has a rival patron, it is them, and it is a trap
Row 6: Made a legend.Accept: The legend takes it instead of their task: 5 parts
Row 6: Made a legend.Twist: Fight: 10 parts, and a rival patron is crossed off / the legend starts the next battle **Shook**, trap or not

Row 6: Made a legend.Event: **The Annual Improvement Awards** nominate the fighter, in a category nobody can explain
Row 6: Made a legend.Accept: The award goes to a harvest figure, and the committee sends a voucher: the first purchase this break costs 2 less
Row 6: Made a legend.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for a better seat: the crew gains **Showboats**, and a judge leaves a copy item worth up to 3 parts
Row 6: Made a legend.Twist: Shoot, Hard (10): the award is a shooting display, and they win it: Fighter of the Year, gain a **lead**, and 7 parts / they hit the harvest figure that won last year: lose the **lead** (the committee drops you from the list)

Row 6: Made a legend.Event: **Imitators.** Someone has the legend's walk, and the legend's hat
Row 6: Made a legend.Accept: A rookie may be hired for 5 parts less; they insist on the same title with a prefix
Row 6: Made a legend.Pay: Pay **2 parts**: hire the imitator free (they still take the prefixed title)
Row 6: Made a legend.Twist: Fight, Routine (6): the legend spars with the imitator and wins, and lends back the hat: hire them for 10 parts less / the imitator wins: the legend starts the next battle **Shook**, and the imitator is written as a **rival**

Row 6: Made a legend.Event: **The legend grows.** By the next camp, the story has a horse in it
Row 6: Made a legend.Accept: A fan sends word, and the word gets about: gain the contact **Fixer**
Row 6: Made a legend.Twist: Nerve: they tell it themselves, and tell it well: gain a **lead**, and the first purchase this break costs 5 less / they oversell it, and a patron stops believing it: lose a **contact**

Row 7: The Bodgers.Event: **The roof comes in.** The wreck-home was held up by tape and hope, and the tape gave up first
Row 7: The Bodgers.Accept: One fighter is **Sore** (they held the beam, and the beam held them)
Row 7: The Bodgers.Pay: Pay **1 part**: a mate turns up with a ladder and a roll of silver, and nobody is hurt
Row 7: The Bodgers.Twist: Tech: you tape it better than it ever was, and the neighbours want theirs taped too: gain the contact **Fixer**, and one fighter starts the next battle **Under warranty** / it falls in again, slower: one fighter is **Sore**, and one copy item is lost under the beam

Row 7: The Bodgers.Event: **Dipstick thinks out loud** about your next fight, all night, one step at a time, and does not skip a step
Row 7: The Bodgers.Accept: Dipstick has not finished, and the power it used is on the crew's bill: recharging costs double this break
Row 7: The Bodgers.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for a flask of something hot: one fighter stays up to listen, and you gain a **lead**
Row 7: The Bodgers.Twist: Tech, Hard (10): you hear the wrong step and say so, out loud, to a machine: gain a **lead** and a copy item worth up to 3 parts / you follow it to the end: one fighter is **Sore** (a long night), and Dipstick bills the power: lose a **contact**

Row 7: The Bodgers.Event: **One of ours is stuck** down a wreck, and calling, in the voice you keep for friends
Row 7: The Bodgers.Accept: You heard nothing, and it eats at the fighter who did: one fighter starts the next battle **Shook**
Row 7: The Bodgers.Pay: Pay **1 part** for a spare cell: the winch runs all night, the Bodger is hauled out, grey and grateful, and the crew gains **Merciful**
Row 7: The Bodgers.Twist: Grit: you haul them out by hand, and they owe you: gain a contact of your choice, and a copy item worth up to 3 parts / the wreck shifts, and the Bodger is still down there. Word goes round the tapes: gain **Ran**

Row 7: The Bodgers.Event: **A claim on your claim** (Red Tape). Another crew has filed against the item you claimed, and has a stamp for it
Row 7: The Bodgers.Accept: Lose one copy item: their paperwork was better, and they say so kindly
Row 7: The Bodgers.Pay: Write the claimant as a **rival**: keep the item, and keep the receipt
Row 7: The Bodgers.Twist: Tech: yours was filed first, and they withdraw with a bow and leave their stamp: gain a **lead** / wrong colour of ink: lose the item, and recharging costs double this break (their name is on the form)

Row 7: The Bodgers.Event: **A collector watches the restoration** (Silver Tape). They stand with their hands behind their back and watch a wreck go from scrap to shine
Row 7: The Bodgers.Accept: The collector tips you in kind, a copy item worth up to 3 parts, and tells nobody, which Silver Tape takes hard
Row 7: The Bodgers.Pay: Pay **1 part** for polish: the collector takes the wreck, and you gain the contact **Fence** and a copy item worth up to 3 parts
Row 7: The Bodgers.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): they love the talk and tell everyone, which is the point: gain a **lead** and a copy item worth up to 3 parts / they ask a question you cannot answer and leave, and word goes round: lose a **contact**

Row 7: The Bodgers.Event: **The pod queue** (Black Tape). It moves a yard a day, and the whole camp is in it, and nobody remembers what for
Row 7: The Bodgers.Accept: You give up your place and watch it close behind you: the first purchase this break costs 2 more
Row 7: The Bodgers.Pay: Pay **3 parts** for a runner who queues all night and befriends the clerk: gain the contact **Friend at the meter**
Row 7: The Bodgers.Twist: Fight: you take the front of the queue, and nobody argues for long: roll on the **finds** table / the queue takes it badly, and word goes round the camps: gain **Ran**

Row 7: The Inspectorate.Event: **Surprise audit.** A superior from another district goes through your papers, one drawer at a time
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Accept: One fighter sits with the auditor and holds the pen all day: they start the next battle **Shook**
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Pay: Pay **1 part** for a clean folder: they vouch for you, nobody sits with the auditor, and the auditor's cousin needs work: one rookie may be hired for 5 parts less
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Twist: Tech: every form is in order, and the auditor leaves a stamped crate: a copy item worth up to 5 parts / a stamp is upside down, and so is the mood: lose the **lead**, and the auditor is written as a **rival**

Row 7: The Inspectorate.Event: **A citizen's complaint** about a fine, in green ink
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Accept: Filed under C, for Complaint: write the citizen on the roster as a **rival**
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Pay: Pay **2 parts** for a handwritten apology: no rival, and the crew gains **Merciful**
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Twist: Nerve, Routine (6): you apologise, and mean it, which confuses the clerk: no rival, the citizen becomes your contact **Informer**, and an old stamp is yours: a copy item worth up to 3 parts / you fine them for complaining, and they appeal: you broke your own apology: gain **Oathbreakers**

Row 7: The Inspectorate.Event: **New hats.** The district issues one size to every crew, from a warehouse that sells nothing else
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Accept: The smallest fighter walks into a post, in the hat: that fighter is **Sore**
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Pay: Pay a tailor **3 parts**: up to three fighters start the next battle **Under warranty** (it fits like armour)
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Twist: Grit: the captain wears two hats and looks it, and the district clerk is impressed: the first purchase this break costs 5 less / the hat catches in the door, with the captain under it: the captain is **Sore**, and recharging costs double this break

Row 7: The Inspectorate.Event: **A merchant and a very heavy crate** (Weights and Measures). They have to cross your scale, and the scale has views
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Accept: The scale says what it says, and nobody argues: the first sale this break is at full price (the scale is on your side)
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Twist: Tech: you lean on the scale, gently: **+8 parts** / the merchant spots it: write them as a **rival**, and give back 3 parts

Row 7: The Inspectorate.Event: **Your annual review** (Department of Improvement). Very cheerful, and printed on Gawk's best paper
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Accept: The Department sends a small grant in kind: recharge one fighter's battery by 2, free
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Pay: The captain swears to improve: a **Small Word**, a vow on their card for the next battle (section 13.5), and the Department sends **4 parts**
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Twist: Nerve: "Exceeds expectations", in a round hand: one fighter starts the next battle **Hyped**, and the first purchase this break costs 5 less / "Needs improvement": the Department sends a trainer, and the captain starts the next battle **Shook** (a week of lectures)

Row 7: The Inspectorate.Event: **A controlled burn** (Fire Marshals). The standing orders say your camp must be set alight once a quarter, for safety, and it is your quarter, and they have brought matches
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Accept: Lose one copy item (it was in the tent)
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Pay: Pay **1 part**: a fighter carries the tent out first, and you lose nothing
Row 7: The Inspectorate.Twist: Grit, Hard (10): you save the lot, through the smoke, and the Marshals pin a medal on the fighter: they start the next battle **Under warranty**, and 4 parts / the fighter is **Sore**, and the item is lost

Row 7: The Waiting.Event: **A heretic at the fire** says the gate is dead, mildly, over the stew
Row 7: The Waiting.Accept: One fighter starts the next battle **Shook** (a doubt is a doubt)
Row 7: The Waiting.Pay: Pay **1 part**: the heretic leaves their coat, a copy armour worth up to 5 parts, and walks on
Row 7: The Waiting.Twist: Nerve: the heretic stays to listen, and knows something: gain a **lead** and a copy armour worth up to 3 parts / you begin to wonder, and the singing sounds thinner: lose the **lead** (the doubt got there first), and recharging costs double this break

Row 7: The Waiting.Event: **A pod lands in the night.** The sky has spoken, and the crew gathers to sing at it
Row 7: The Waiting.Accept: The crew sings at it all night, and nobody opens it, and the priest leaves an offering: 2 parts
Row 7: The Waiting.Pay: One fighter opens it and is **Sore** (a week of penance for the blasphemy): roll on the **drop** table (section 11.7). An arrival from it joins as usual
Row 7: The Waiting.Twist: Nerve: the priest blesses it first, at length: roll on the drop table, and nobody does penance / the sky is displeased: the fighter who opened it is **Sore**, and the pod is empty

Row 7: The Waiting.Event: **A relic with a plaque** turns up in the baggage: VOID IF REMOVED
Row 7: The Waiting.Accept: It was removed, and the priest has seen the empty hook, and tells the camp: lose a **contact**
Row 7: The Waiting.Pay: Pay **4 parts** for a plaque remover: gain a **relic tip** (section 14.7)
Row 7: The Waiting.Twist: Nerve, Hard (10): the priest knows what it is, and kneels: one relic may be bought this break at half price, with no roll for a seller, and gain a **relic tip** / it was a desk bell: lose a **contact**, one fighter starts the next battle **Shook**, and the priest writes the crew down as a **rival**

Row 7: The Waiting.Event: **The answer, word for word** (the Listeners). A Listener told a stranger what the voice said, as their own thought, and the stranger acted on it
Row 7: The Waiting.Accept: The stranger turns up, hungry, and cites you: lose 2 parts
